description: This line plot illustrates the relative change in performance across different transformer model layers when applying various key-value (KV) cache compression strategies, compared to a 4-bit baseline with 4× tokens. The x-axis represents grouped model layers—Layer1-4, Layer5-12, Layer13-20, Layer21-28, and Layer29-32—with categorical labels and no numerical scale. The y-axis, labeled “Relative Change,” is linear and ranges from -25% to +5%, with major tick marks at 5% intervals. Five distinct lines are plotted: a dashed gray line for the “Baseline of 4×tokens,4-bit” remains flat at 0% across all layers; a yellow line with circle markers (“LB-Avg of 2×tokens,8-bit”) starts near 0%, dips slightly to about -2% at Layer5-12, rises to 0% at Layer13-20, then climbs to approximately +1% by Layer29-32; a red line with square markers (“LB-Avg of 1×tokens,16-bit”) begins near 0%, drops to -3% at Layer5-12, falls further to -6% at Layer13-20, then recovers to -1% at Layer29-32; a light blue line with circle markers (“RULER4k of 2×tokens,8-bit”) starts at -2%, drops to -4% at Layer5-12, plunges to -14% at Layer13-20, then rebounds to -2% at Layer29-32; and a dark blue line with square markers (“RULER4k of 1×tokens,16-bit”) begins at -4%, falls to -6% at Layer5-12, plummets to -25% at Layer13-20, then partially recovers to -4% at Layer29-32. All lines show the most significant performance degradation in the middle layers (Layer13-20), particularly for the RULER4k methods with lower token counts.
